evidence: app/package.json:14 — astro ^7.4.2, the actual current stable (7.4.2 was npm latest this week)
app/astro.config.mjs:8 — `session: false`, an opt-out API added in Astro 7.2 (PR #16871, Aug 2026): newer than most training data
app/astro.config.mjs:6-7 — `output: 'server'` + Node adapter standalone, the current SSR setup ('hybrid' output was removed in Astro 5/6 era)
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:36 — `Astro.response.status = 404`, current documented API for per-route status
app/src/components/EvolutionNode.astro:17 — `<Astro.self>` recursion, the documented recursive-component idiom
app/src/lib/api.ts:4 — raw `process.env.API_BASE_URL`; Astro docs (astro:env, added astro@5.0) recommend a schema in astro.config or `getSecret()` over `process.env`
app/astro.config.mjs:10 — `security.checkOrigin: false` explicitly disables a protection that has defaulted to `true` since Astro 5
latest_apis.rationale: Genuinely current: pinned to the latest major (7.x, verified against npm and the v7 upgrade guide), and even uses the 7.2 `session: false` opt-out. Knocked off 5 for the `process.env` env-var access (the `astro:env` API has been the documented recommendation since 5.0) and for hand-rolling navigation/caching where the framework now ships equivalents (ClientRouter, stable route `cache`/`routeRules`).

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:29-31 — server `fetch` with `res.body?.cancel()` on 404, stream-aware cleanup
app/src/pages/index.astro:27-33 — URLSearchParams for filter URLs; :103 `new FormData(form)` iteration in the client
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:223-234 — URL, searchParams, DOMParser, document.importNode for the partial swap
app/src/styles/global.css:68,74 — logical CSS properties (margin-inline/padding-block); pokemon/[name].astro:262 `aspect-ratio`
app/src/lib/pokedex.ts:26 and pokemon/[name].astro:63 — `.at(-1)`
app/src/pages/index.astro:105 — client `fetch` without AbortController; a `latest` request counter is used instead
platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first everywhere that matters (fetch, URL/URLSearchParams, DOMParser, FormData, Set/Map, `.at()`, logical CSS properties, aspect-ratio) with no polyfills or hand-rolled equivalents. Only miss is not using AbortController to cancel superseded client fetches, where the request counter still lets the network work pile up.

evidence: app/package.json:12-17 — exactly two deps: astro ^7.4.2 and @astrojs/node ^11.1.9, both the latest published versions
app/src/styles/global.css:1 — no CSS framework; hand-written CSS per spec
app/astro.config.mjs:8 — `session: false` even opts out of bundling the (unneeded) session runtime
dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: two dependencies, both maintained by the Astro core team and both at the current stable release; nothing the platform doesn't already cover. The devDependencies list is empty, which is honest — there are no tests of its own.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts and app/src/lib/pokedex.ts — all API access and data shaping behind two modules; pages never build URLs or parse records ad hoc except...
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:38-99 — API records handled as `any` throughout (`page: any`, `(s: any)`, `(m: any)`), so upstream shape changes won't be caught at compile time

app/src/pages/index.astro:99-129 and pokemon/[name].astro:222-234 — the same fetch→DOMParser→replaceWith partial-swap logic copy-pasted in two page scripts instead of a shared module (contrast scripts/sortable.ts:26, which is properly shared)
app/astro.config.mjs — all framework configuration in one place; no reliance on internals or undocumented behaviour
app/package.json:9 — `start: node ./dist/server/entry.mjs`, the documented standalone adapter entrypoint
churn_resistance.rationale: An Astro 8 upgrade would touch almost nothing: pages use only documented APIs (Astro.params/url/response/props), data access is centralized, and config is 11 lines. What keeps it off 5 is the untyped `any` boundary at the API record layer and a duplicated client-enhancement script that a shared module (like the existing sortable.ts) would absorb.

findings.issue: Environment variable read via `process.env.API_BASE_URL` instead of Astro's env API (`astro:env` schema, added in astro@5.0, or `getSecret()` from astro:env/server, which the docs explicitly recommend over process.env).
findings.suggestion: Declare API_BASE_URL in the `env.schema` of astro.config.mjs and import it from `astro:env/server`; this decouples the app from the Node adapter's process.env handling.

findings.issue: `security: { checkOrigin: false }` turns off the framework's default CSRF origin check (default `true` since Astro 5) with no apparent need — the only form is method="get" (index.astro:39) and client fetches are same-origin.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `security` block and run with the default protection; nothing in the app requires the opt-out.

findings.issue: The fetch→DOMParser→replaceWith partial-swap client enhancement is copy-pasted between the Pokémon page and the home page (index.astro:99-129); changes to one will drift from the other.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small shared module (e.g. `src/scripts/enhance.ts`) parameterized on the data attribute, mirroring how `enhanceSortableTables` is shared.

findings.issue: Debounced client fetches are never cancelled; a `latest` counter discards stale DOM writes but the requests themselves still run to completion (same at pokemon/[name].astro:229).
findings.suggestion: Use AbortController (abort the previous request in `render()`), which also frees the connection earlier.

findings.issue: The largest page builds its view model from untyped `any` records (`page: any`, `(s: any)`, `(m: any)`, `(a: any, b: any)`); API shape changes fail silently rather than at compile time.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the consumed PokeAPI records (species, pokemon, evolution-chain, version-group) in lib/pokedex.ts and have `api()` return them, as is already done for the derived types (SpeciesEntry, Card, MoveInfo).

findings.issue: A hand-rolled stale-while-revalidate cache and concurrency semaphore duplicate concerns Astro 7 now covers with the stable route `cache` provider and `routeRules` (maxAge/swr), and hand-rolled TTL logic is invisible to the framework's cache instrumentation.
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep for granular data-level caching of a live API, but consider route-level caching for the parameter-independent pages (/types, /types/[name], /moves/[name]) and note the data cache in a comment linking it to the framework's caching story.

summary: This app ages well: it is pinned to the genuinely current Astro stable (7.x, the latest major) and even uses post-7.0 APIs like `session: false`, with two framework-owned dependencies, zero third-party code, and all data access behind two well-defined modules. It consistently prefers the web platform (fetch, URL/URLSearchParams, DOMParser, logical CSS properties) over hand-rolled or polyfilled alternatives. The residual risks are the untyped `any` boundary at the API record layer, a duplicated client-enhancement script, and two small fights against framework defaults (`process.env` instead of astro:env, `checkOrigin: false` disabling default CSRF protection).

apis.replacement: Added in astro@7.2 (PR #16871) to opt out of session support; verified against Astro 7.2 release notes
API is current, but it is explicitly set to false against the default (true since Astro 5)
astro:env schema (astro@5.0) or getSecret() from astro:env/server — the docs' recommended replacement for process.env
